events.text: my friend Tanvi's landlord wants to raise her rent 9% next year. it's a condo in liberty village, built 2010 i think. is that even legal in ontario?

events.name: Bash

input.command: web search "Ontario rent increase guideline 2026 units occupied before November 2018"

events.output:
1. Rent increase guideline | ontario.example.ca
   The 2026 rent increase guideline is 2.1%. It applies to most private residential rental units, including rented condominium units, first occupied for residential purposes before November 15, 2018.
2. Above guideline increases (AGI) | Landlord and Tenant Board
   A landlord must apply to the LTB to raise rent above the guideline, for example after major capital repairs. Tenants can dispute the application at a hearing.
3. Notice of rent increase (Form N1) | tribunalsontario.example.ca
   Landlords must give at least 90 days' written notice, and rent can only go up once every 12 months.

events.text:
No, not without LTB approval. A 2010 condo is covered by rent control, so for 2026 the cap is the 2.1% guideline.
- Units first occupied before 15 Nov 2018 are capped; hers qualifies.
- Anything above 2.1% needs an above-guideline increase approved by the Landlord and Tenant Board, which she can contest.
- The landlord must give 90 days' written notice on Form N1, and only once every 12 months.
- If she gets an N1 for 9% with no LTB application, she can simply pay the guideline amount.

Want me to put the links and a short summary in a note she can use?

Morse Street PS notice: The first day of school is Tuesday, September 8, 2026. Class lists will be posted on Edsby on Friday, September 4 after 15:00. Kindergarten staggered entry schedule is attached. Before-and-after-care registration closes Monday, August 24.
